quoteAlternatives.quote: What a wonder it is! So grand, so solemn, so vast! And yet so delicate, so airy, so graceful! A very world of solid weight, and yet it seems in the soft moonlight only a fairy delusion of frost-work that might vanish with a breath!
quoteAlternatives.attribution: Mark Twain, writer, The Innocents Abroad (1869)
quoteAlternatives.note: Full sentence of option 1. Twain is describing the Duomo cathedral, not the city as a whole.

quoteAlternatives.quote: Arrigo Beyle, Milanese. Scrisse, amò, visse.
quoteAlternatives.attribution: Stendhal, novelist, his own epitaph (“Henri Beyle, Milanese. He wrote, he loved, he lived.”)
quoteAlternatives.note: The French novelist chose to be called Milanese on his grave in Montmartre Cemetery, Paris. In Italian; would need the translation shown.
